author: Azcron
subject: Re: Minimum requirements to join BGS
content_md:
> **amanagor wrote: Mon Apr 06, 2026 8:42 am**
> Firstly, AV is not a real bg, it should removed from the game. Secondly, players should be forced to participate in an equal number of AB games than wsg games (cant queue for one if they have over 5 more games in the other bg).
>  Thirdly, there should be a minimum requirement of skill to join bgs. For example, for wsg, People that don't know the basic jumps should not be allowed to queue. To teach the jumps, put in place a custom empty map for people to practice.

 1. Just because it’s large‑scale and objective‑heavy doesn’t make it ‘not real.’ It’s part of WoW’s PvP DNA.

 2. Forcing players to queue WSG and AB in equal numbers would be a disaster. WSG has always been the least‑popular BG, and forcing people into content they don’t enjoy doesn’t improve PvP, it just increases AFKs and resentment. If a battleground needs mandatory participation to stay alive, that says more about the battleground than the players.

 3. Making movement exploits a requirement to queue? That’s backwards. Jumps and wall‑tech are fun tricks but, you’re basically suggesting that engine quirks from 20 years ago should gatekeep who’s allowed to PvP. Battlegrounds should reward actual gameplay skill, not punish people for not knowing niche terrain exploits.

author: Urthius
subject: Re: Loosen faction balance thresholds on Tel'abim
content_md:
My main argument is that we should be looking at PvP activity to determine faction balance, not raw character counts. Expecting Ally and Horde to PvP at similar rates is a reasonable default assumption, but empirically isn't true.

For example: every 15 minutes, count how many Ally/Horde are either in BGs or queued for BGs. Take weekly averages and adjust faction balancing based on that. On Tel'Abim, I suspect that the skew is 60/40 in favor of Horde, at least.

If this is the case, it doesn't make sense to lock Ally character creation, especially when the server needs more population.

Other metrics should also be considered, of course, including raw character counts. But something like the example above should definitely be a factor.

There is a lag between when players join and when they are PvP active, so any changes should be conservative.

The slippery slope can be avoided by making decisions based on such data.

author: ForumGentleman
subject: SAVE TEL ABIM Server
content_md:
**Clearly, Tel Abim is not going through a good phase right now.**

Stuck at 1k-1.5k pop... definitely not enough for a PvP server. Server needs at least 2.5k/3k to have constant PvP.

BGs are quite rare these days. World PvP? Barely a thing.

So, what do we do?  **What can the DEVS do?**

A slow trickle of new players is not gonna cut it. The other two servers have too much inertia and their high pop is a big appeal, even to normally PvP-minded players.

My suggestions are:

- Unique features for the server – PvP and world PvP unique content: world PvP quests, capturable objectives with faction-wide buffs, world PvP specific rewards, destroyable minor cities, loot on faction leaders... There are plenty of ideas, some of which don't require too much work.

- Promoting the server – on the server selection screen obviously, possibly also with a dedicated YouTube video (once we get unique features). Maybe giving a limited XP boost for a couple of months?

- Cross-server BGs – I honestly don't like the idea, but maybe it could help the server until it reaches a self-sustaining population.

- Free one-way transfer from other servers to Tel Abim – also controversial, maybe just for a limited time?

What do you guys think? Any other suggestions?

author: Bjorn88
subject: Re: SAVE TEL ABIM Server
content_md:
TA went from ca 1500 to ca 3k pop over the summer period last year. Then, devs decided to open a new server in Ambershire. My guess is that a lot of the newer TA players went to Amber instead.

I was expecting 18.1 to increase pvp activity due to the pvp gear, wpvp events, etc. What's happened on TA is that the faction imbalance of pvpers in the playerbase has become much more evident. Locked faction balance is a good thing on paper, but if the alliance players dont que bgs, we are stuck with de facto imbalance in the pvp playerbase.

A major reason alliance players dont que, according to some of them, is class imbalance. Shaman tank talents are consistently pointed out as the issue. Class imbalances are a known issue on twow and it doesn't help when you are trying to advertise a server to wow pvp players. Devs need to start considering pvp seriously when class changes are made. Dampening is a bandaid, not a solution.

TA has a great community and playerbase, it just get consistently shit on by poor management and game design decisions that work on a xfaction pve server but not a pvp server.

And yes, at this stage TA needs to have some unique pvp-related features that will draw players to it.

I wouldn't say wpvp is "barely a thing" though, last week Alliance raided OG with 70+ people and held the city for nearly an hour:
[embed: https://www.youtube.com/embed/afZNbCuWvl4]

This is the kind of content many are looking for when they roll on a pvp server. Sadly, beyond the fun and the hks, there is not much material incentive to organize these kinds of raids. Wpvp-related quests/challenges, faction leader loot/rewards, that are unique for TA can go a long way.

content_md:
Some good feedback around here... and some lame ones.

Honestly getting tired of hearing some shit arguments. People need to realize:

- **THERE WAS NEVER PERFECT BALANCE**. Ever, in any expansion. You can't have perfect balance with 9 classes, dozens of different specs, different PvP setups (BGs, duels, world PvP, arena), and professions. It's just too many variables. Saying people don't play PvP because there's no perfect balance is just stupid.

- **NO, Horde is not organically stronger in PvP than Alliance RIGHT NOW.** We had broken paladins for years, and then yes, we got really strong shamans, which got nerfed last patch (the problematic 10% damage reduction). Right now, neither side is broken and it's actually quite balanced.

- **No, ACTUAL PvPers don't stop playing because of gear differences. What the hell?** This mentality is really coming from PvE crybabies, I swear. You think Vurtne, who made his career killing T3 players while in blue gear, cried about gear difference? Real PvPers don't give up on a fucking challenge whether facing more geared players or doing 1vX.
That's the beauty of vanilla (and Turtle WoW): even undergeared, many matchups are still doable.

- No, fixing a couple stats here and there on PvP gear is not gonna fix the problem. Stop acting like that minor fucking thing is the main reason.

- **YES, PvE players also cry about the slightest LAME thing.** New dungeon too hard? Cry. New dungeon too easy? Cry. A minor change of +5 intellect on their preferred set? Cry. So what? All players cry about shit things. What's your point bringing that up?

 **Now, can we go back to good suggestions on HOW TO SAVE TEL ABIM AND THE PVP SCENE?**

content_md:
TA's history has been marked by poor timing from the devs.

First, the server opened a month before SoD was released on 2023. TA pop was around 4k just before the opening iirc.
Then, it proceeded to drop to ca 300 in the summer of 2024.
In the latter half of 2024 and early 2025, pop gradually rose to ca 12-1500.

Over the summer of 2025, pop rose from 1500 to 3000.

Then, what do devs do? Release Ambershire. It's pretty clear that a majority of the new TA players rerolled there.
TA since has dropped from 2200 peaks to 16-1700 as we have now.

The opening of Ambershire really was poor timing if devs wanted to keep TA up. Wait half a year, and the new wave of players would have been more consolidated on TA.

Moreover it doesn't help that TA gets affected negatively by sharing code with crossfaction pve servers, e.g:
 1) no faction-specific loot tables (i.e. horde continues to get paladin loot despite bug reports and vice versa)
 2) new ranking formula being based on crossfaction insta-ques, and not adapted to horde-alliance ques on TA
 3) horrendous class balance which pushes dedicated pvp'ers away from the server

With all that, what is the purpose for them to keep going with the PvP-Route? What's the gain, except for hate and unhappy PvP-Players? They're only draining themselves. author: Cellion
subject: New tier of trunks from fishing
content_md:
One of the nice little treats while fishing from pools is getting a Watertight Trunk or equivalent. These cool little boxes pop out a small amount of cloth and leather and some consumables, plus a small chance at a green crafting material or gear piece.

The highest level trunk currently is the Mithril Bound Trunk, which grants gear for levels 35-45, and level 30-40 potions, with mostly mageweave and thick leather (and a small chance for runecloth and rugged leather). Unfortunately once you get into levels 45+ these trunks stop being particularly interesting.

I think it would be awesome if there was one more tier of Trunk for the highest level bracket. These could come from the level 50+ zones and contain level 45-55 gear, level 40+ potions, some of the higher tier gems, and more regular runecloth and rugged leather.

Seeing as this will probably be the next big patch I wanted to leave some of my suggestions for it. First of all based on the lore and the location it should be heavily based on the Forsaken(Horde side) and High Elf(Alliance side) lore. This is a perfect time to expand on the undead and high elf/blood elf lore with really fun quest and stories and focus on WC3. I feel like this patch can be the RP dream if done right and should have some RP updates(like new player customization options, new gear, new pets, new mounts...) at the very least. I  aware that Amani trolls will play a big part in this patch also but please don't hand horde just another quest hub with muddy huts, we can be more creative than that. Since we will be walking on scourge infested ground it would be really cool if we could get some cool Scourge gear, masks and hoods, undead horses and such and it would be really fun to make it all actually scary and creepy, basically a horror expansion if you will with a darker tone that reflects the occasional grimness of warcraft. I really can't wait to play this patch and I hope that it's as good if not even better than all the last ones.

Probably the fact that self-proclaimed PvP players are some of the most insufferable people to be around, and I have better things to do in life than be surrounded by people who would probably be more than happy to gut an entire game in the name of getting their "Fuck you I want PvP" fix.

Esit: I still like to get into PvP now and then, but to a much lesser degree than I did when I was younger. I've grown to appreciate immersion over clubbing people over the head in my games, especially when the thing you see coming from people is "Stop wasting time on making content and just work on PvP!!!!!"

author: Troggyboy
subject: Just remove 2x EXP from Tel'Abim . . .
content_md:
I know this isn't exactly what everyone wants but I feel like it's one of the main reasons the server's population is so low.

Presumably it's on here because the devs think PvP players don't care that much about grinding and want to spend less time doing it and more time just fighting other players in the open world or BGs. But honestly, this isn't the reason why I joined Tel'Abim. For me, it's the thrill and the action of engaging with other players while questing and being in the open world, it's the salt for the stew, without which it would be rather bland.

But if you're that brand of player, Tel'Abim isn't ideal. Since so many people only care about getting to 60 on here, people quest faster, there are fewer people around to begin with AND the population is kind of split between WPvP players and BG players, this drastically reduces the amount of players from the other faction you can actually run into in the open world.

You can technically turn off EXP gains for yourself by doing the Slow and Steady challenge or turning on .xpmode but in reality that doesn't quite work either. For some reason it ignores the EXP gained from quests which means that those still give you too much, leaving you overleveled anyway, especially early on. This has been known for a long time and gets complained about by new players finding out in world chat pretty much every other day but it still has yet to be adressed and I honestly believe it has cost Tel'Abim a lot of players who would've stuck around otherwise.

But personally, I'd go even further and just remove those EXP gains entirely. The game has been designed with normal EXP rates in mind, both the classic content aswell as all of the new turtle stuff. It's entirely too jarring and imbalanced when the EXP gets doubled and it just takes away from the game imo, and I truly believe the population is so low because many other players feel the same and NOT because people dislike PvP servers.

With that being said, there are of course people who still want to have the 2x EXP and come to the server for that specifically. But there are other ways of letting them have it, like perhaps adjusting War Mode to serve their needs without it affecting the entire server, just to mention one idea.

This is not the only issue the server has - for one there's the aforementioned split between WPvP and BG players which gives the server a somewhat schizophrenic identity, making it hard to adress the needs of one side without also inadvertently making it worse for the other. Or the problems PvP servers have always had, like adressing excessive griefing without taking away from the spirit of the server or gaining you more from engaging in WPvP than just doing it for the love of the game. But adressing the 2x EXP issue or at the very least just fixing .xpmode and Slow and Steady would already be a great start.

Alright that's all I wanted to say, thank you for reading everyone.

War Mode gives exp because war mode as a concept was taken from retail and then adjusted. On retail, it also gives exp.

In both cases, I guess it's to incentivise people to pick it and win over the PvE players to also try it, who make up the majority of the playerbase.

I suppose war mode actually makes more sense on retail, because retail no longer has dedicated PvP servers. This was also the case for TWoW before Tel'Abim, but after it came out, most of the dedicated PvP'ers simply went there (I'd presume).

That said, IIRC, War Mode on TWoW used to give even more exp and less honour, and they lowered the exp gain and increased the honour gain.

content_md:

> Imagine paladins will want their favourite class on both sides. And what about shamams.

I mean, hypothetically you could give each side a class that plays similarly but is thematically different. Like putting Death Knights on Horde (not the Wrath version, but an actual Paladin-equivalent based on its RTS appearances) and then giving Alliance some sort of class that works around...I don't know...smaller runestones, rather than totems. I take your meaning, though. For an idea to work, it has to be balanced and have the right flavour.

That said...instead of just going, "But what about X?" let's try to theorycraft here.

You want Naga, right? I think that Naga would be a race that could actually be a Druid on Horde side, given their common ancestry with elves (though for that matter, Trolls could also be justified as Druid, just learning their forms from different Loa, by much the same logic). Sure, Naga don't have legs, but Trolls don't have shoes show up on their models either.

For Alliance, maybe a tribe of Furbolgs that has fled the corruption taking their race. Or Dryads, who were a part of the Night Elf faction in WCIII. Either one would be a race with ties to the Alliance, via the Night Elves, and who has strong ties to nature. Furbolgs have the advantage of already being known to have several character classes that exist in game, including Druids, but would be a little difficult to model armour for. Dryads would be easier, but have fewer obvious class options, and like Naga there's the issue of either needing special lower body armour or having it not show on the model.

author: Alexianon
subject: Visual distinction for upgraded items on the auction house
content_md:
Currently, the auction house displays upgraded items (enchanted, socketed, etc.) exactly the same as ordinary ones in the search list. Sellers undercut each other by a single copper, while items with real added value are ignored simply because they are not visible at first glance.

Suggestion:
Modify the server so that upgraded items receive a visual marker in the standard auction house list. For example: a different text color, small icon or special frame or border.

Buyers can instantly see which items have real improvements, crafters and enchanters gain a fair advantage for their work. This encourages crafting and adds value to the economy.

This is not about adding complex filters or changing how the auction works. Just a visual hint.

Sincerely

author: Sylerann
subject: Playtesting!
content_md:
Hey devs, if you happen to be reading this, I'm writing to suggest some sort of playtesting for content.

Of course I assume the devs themselves test things ingame to some extent, but the scope of that is clearly limited, and this could be supplemented with a group of volunteer playtesters. Different skill levels, play styles and class mains.

I believe plenty of people would be more than happy to give feedback on new patches and alert developers to glaring issues or missteps in balance, in order to have a better release. The new content has been incredible but certain changes are simply suffering from a lack of quality control.

For example- It's difficult to believe anyone testing changes has given balance druid or rogue a good test drive. The 'buff' that's actually a nerf to druid, and the incredibly obnoxious poison management would have immediately raised the alarm on a playtester of these classes at an intermediate level. There are other questionable PvE decisions (shaman) but these two illustrate my point pretty well.

I could go on about other easily reported issues- there's still a tunnel after archdruid in Timbermaw Hold that crashes the game if you pass through it, to mention another. It could possibly be haunted. I don't think that's necessary, though.

The point is, many people want to see this project succeed, and they want to help. The aggressiveness and outward frustration of critics is just due to a lack of dialogue between the development staff and community. It would even help to just let people know you acknowledge a mistake.

content_md:
Isn't it the legendary that requires the most luck? Someone can HR it each reset and if unlucky, they still won't have it. Atiesh is much easier to get if you really want to obtain it because the splinters are predictable drop. Scythe is pure RNG just like Bindings. I think that even both Bindings are easier to get than Scythe because of higher drop chance. And yet some guilds complain they can't get any TF for half a year.

With that being said, I see many players flexing with Scythe in Orgrimmar. I don't know how they are so lucky.

I did some math.

Assuming that you are the only one player HRing Scythe in Kara10 and you clear it every 5 days for 1 year, you have a chance of almost 23% of no Scythe drop.

Assuming you are the only one who HRs it and you clear MC every 7 days for 1 year, you have a chance of 7% of no Bindings drop. However, this takes into account only rarer Bindings. I assume there is oversupply of the left one because of higher drop chance.

author: Xudo
subject: Re: Ambershire warcaches, economy
content_md:
Economy changes were done because almost every year (probably after content patches) people massively complained about high prices for consumables.

You can find reason why devs implemented caches with consumables in old economy updates:
[PvP & Economy Update](https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?t=12138) - it was the first attempt to intervene economy to reduce prices for consumables.
[Economy Update — Consumables & Gold Farming](https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?t=12931) - elixirs now persist through death
[Economy Update — Nodes, Trash & Consumables](https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?t=13448) - they nerfed gold income from lashers.
[Economy Update — GDKP, TDKP, and Turtle WoW](https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?t=12932)

In short - people in raids spend enormous amount of effort to get all consumables possible.
Because of high demand for consumables and low supply of natural herbs in open world, people started to farm lashers.
With lashers they also farmed raw gold, which indirectly increased prices for everything.
Some guilds used to grant items to players for gold. It also encouraged people to farm gold. Best way to farm gold was to farm herbs and sell them.

So all game was reduced to farming lashers, which is not that turtle devs wanted.
Turtle devs added war caches to give people alternative to farming lashers. People can participate in normal dungeon boss killing and get consumables.

I don't exactly know why caches contain final products. Maybe there are additional reasons for that.

Even as someone who was looking forward to the advantage of making more consumes for myself and not having to worry about buying them through herb/alch, I feel like keeping some sort of cache system that lets players at least have the materials to make potions or have other people make potions is alright. This can also lead to more social economic interactions because, obviously, not everyone is going to have alchemy or a character that has it. They'll need someone else to refine the material into a product. Pretty fun multiplayer experience, right?

author: Zeran
subject: Re: Scaling Dungeons
content_md:
There's a possible side effect here: people won't level any alts and will just do all content on their level 60 chars, which will increase Q times for everyone.

Yes, maybe it other 60's are also Q'ing the same dungeon it won't be so bad, but there's no guarantee they will be Q'ing that exact same dungeon. Whereas when you are in e.g. a level 14-20 level range, there are only a few dungeons you can do, so it narrows it down and helps Q times.

So yeah, in the end, it increases Q times.

author: Azkaul
subject: New Weapon Type: Buckler
content_md:
The Buckler: A Renaissance Shield Begging for Implementation
![Image](https://encrypted-tbn0.gstatic.com/images?q=tbn:ANd9GcRTpWaBYSrNgbc18fQ8rHRrd-BbQd1Bd0boYw&s)

WHY
I've thought about this for a long time, as early as back in Vanilla, and I've always wondered why Shields are just "Shields", whilst Swords, Axes and Maces are 1h and 2h variants. Now I'm not asking for two-handed shields... At least not in this post.

I've long felt that there should be a middle ground between the "your damage kinda sucks now" choice of using a shield over DW or 2H builds, and playing buckler-rapier builds in games like Dark Souls and Elden Ring have only enhanced my hunger for this playstyle and aesthetic, long after the release of Vanilla WoW. **A middle ground that would allow for a fair increase in survivability without committing to full-tank status, whilst also being able to deal decent albeit fairly reduced damage.**

The Aesthetic of The Buckler fits perfectly into the "Magical High-Fantasy Renaissance" World of Azeroth, a world with rudimentary firearms, cannons, naval combat and exploration, pirates and fantastic clashes of cultures.

WHAT
Bucklers are a fantastic piece of late Medieval and Renaissance weaponry, evolving from early Roman influences like the Parma (pictured below)
![Image](https://deepeeka.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/ah6129_standard_bearer_s_parma_dia_24_inch.jpg)
Roman Parma

The intent of the shield is clear at first glance: This isn't your standard Legionnaire's hulking "Scutum" shield, designed for lines of big sweaty 'Joe Rogan's' to form impenetrable (albeit heavy) turtle-shells out of, and then shimmy towards European Barbarians, before giving them a good stabbing with a Gladius.
It's a shield designed to deflect strikes rather than absorb them, and then allow the wielder to give their opponent a good bell-ringing with the metal nose where possible.

In short: **The Buckler is a hybrid shield that is a trio of deflective, protective and offensive.**
Naturally its raw block ability is a shadow of what a proper shield can achieve, but its ability to enhance parry opportunities plus its nature as what is effectively a large set of knuckle-dusters with a tiny shield attached makes it a fascinating opportunity for some expanded class abilities.

HOW
Anyone familiar with shield-using classes has likely noticed quite a large number of shields are actually tiny and in many cases even literally refer to themselves as "[something] Buckler of the [whatever]", these Shields largely already exist in the game but thus-far simply lightning-rod to the base role of "Shield", and all that goes with it.

My proposal for the role of bucklers is this:
- Shield: Significantly reduced block amount, probably 25% of normal shields. Maybe as low as 10%
- Parry: Increased Parry Chance by a small amount (should not be enough to simply replace the damage mitigation of the block nerf, otherwise it's just exactly as good as a hulking great shield)
- Weapon: Acts as a weak off-hand fist-weapon. Likely with a 20% damage nerf on a raw off-hand weapon
- Riposte: Doubles next auto-attack speed after you parry.
Some thoughts on potential scaling;
- Agility could increase parry chance by some % per point whilst using a buckler, making it a more viable tanking alternative.
- The nullification of crits and crushing blows could be reduced or removed entirely for this item

WHO?
My initial thoughts are that this new weapon would be used primarily by **Warriors, Shaman**, and **Rogues** who have a medium-depth-investment in the Combat Tree.
Although there's some historical instances in which Clergy (**Priests**) may have used these with maces (as they were unable to shed blood), so it may be worth putting it deep into the Discipline tree as well.
There is also potentially an argument for **Hunters** to use it as well, as I'll explain in 'The Aesthetic'

Paladins are hulking great titans of The Light and so *do not concern themselves with the dashing finesse of such devices*, although I could be convinced otherwise.

THE AESTHETIC
The Aesthetic of this is simple; the lightly armoured musketeer, switching from gun to rapier and buckler in close combat, the dashing rogue fencing his way through adventures, the warrior loose on the field of battle with a buckler and a rapier running through the enemy.
![Image](https://i.ibb.co/nM511ZkW/ZZZZ.png)

Lore-wise, this would be a cultural import from the fallen Gilnaeus, who are heavy users of muskets, rapiers, bucklers and Renaissance-to-Victorian aesthetic weaponry.

In each instance they prioritize finesse over the kind of raw 'tankiness' associated with The Legionnaire, The Man-at-Arms or The Medieval Plate-Armored Knight.

 - **For Warriors**; this implies light dungeon tanking with increased threat generation that meets in the middle of out-and-out Fury Dual-Wield tanking, with additional utility in levelling and world exploration.

 - **For the Rogue**; it's a chance to add a whole new fantasy role that I believe Combat Spec was always destined to offer, rather than what it is; a scuffed up Fury Warrior. Again, with world-exploration, off-tanking, and potential pvp use.

 - **For the Hunter**; they can act as true Musketeers did, tactically switching (much in the same way Warriors do now) to close combat when the situation calls, and this scales amazingly and synergizes with their existing high parry abilities, making them a reasonable threat up-close, and a danger if you end up facing a flurry of high-speed attacks from them after a number of parries.

 - **For the Shaman**; smacking enemies in the mouth with element-infused fist strikes in the off-hand whilst deflecting blows, giving a fair alternative to pure 2H enhancement builds, and an enhancement tree that could be modified to give this hybrid style of combat more interesting synergies (e.g. pop a Shield unit on parry, Block and Parry chance scale equally to make them more tanky and so on).

There are offhand frills with dodge chance and/or armor.

A buckler just doesnt provide meaningful gameplay appart from whats already covered by shields or defensive offhand frills.

Rogue has a realistic shot at getting immune to melee damge for extended periods of time if he gets access to a significant amount of extra parry chance, and druid reaches the armorcap with a big fat slab of armor.

So if we cant have armor or dodge/parry in high quantities, and it should not encourage a blocking playstile, mathematically a buckler ends up with the same stat distribution as an offhand frill...

author: Kefke
subject: Re: New Weapon Type: Buckler
content_md:
Something that I thought of is this. Based on the codifying of "Vampirism" as a stat, Turtle isn't above adding new attributes to gear to encourage more varied gameplay. So, let me propose a new stat: Counter.

Mechanically, this would give you a bonus to your next attack after foiling an enemy attack. Mainly meaning parry, but I think expanding it to dodge wouldn't be unreasonable either. It could be as simple as a 1-1 bonus to your Str stat. So with a buckler, you'd get a worse shield, but whenever your opponent fails to hit you, you do more damage. Essentially trading reliable defence for unreliable offence (which can be made more reliable with the right build). A middle-of-the-road option in between using a proper shield and dual wielding.

TBH PvP in MMO's is an unsolved problem. I don't know a single MMO where the players are happy with it - it's just hard to balance because the game has both PvE and PvP aspects, so you have to jump through hoops and segregate the two even though that will never be 100% possible, as it might as well become 2 separate games.

The games where PvP is actually easier to balance are genres made specifically for it - like MOBAs, where you can focus on an even playing field and it makes the design that much more streamlined.

author: Lane13
subject: Bestial Discipline and its interaction with Poison Spit
content_md:
Bestial Discipline is a BM talent that currently reduces the CD of pet special abilities by 20% and gives them 5 extra Focus per tick.

Ignoring the fact that the talent needs a buff such as it affecting *all* pet abilities and/or providing more Focus because, due to the bloat of talent points in the BM tree and Bestial Discipline's overall lower damage boost, it's the first one to be skipped if going deep BM... the talent has an additional problem.

Reducing the CD of certain abilities is actually detrimental because of the way they work and the main ability in question here is the serpent's Poison Spit. Poison Spit is a DoT that lasts 8 seconds and also has an 8 second CD. Bestial Discipline lowers the CD and so the serpent constantly overwrites the previous DoT with a new one.

The solution: let each application of Poison Spit be an independent debuff on the target so that if a second one is cast, the damage on the first one that is about to fall off is not totally lost.

subject: Re: Bestial Discipline and its interaction with Poison Spit
content_md:
A similar issue is with Furious Howl. The additional focus is not enough to allow for Bite and Furious Howl to go off naturally while off-CD. In a longer fight, FH will be usually delayed by 1-2 ticks, because Bite ate up the pet's focus. On the surface it may not seem big, but throughout the course of a long fight it adds up. So if you want to have FH available, you have to manually cast your pet's bite and monitor available focus.

I know pet macroing is part of the class, but Bestial Discipline is supposed to remove oddities like that

author: Halfgeek9
subject: PvP dmg debuff is insane 20-30%, on top of "resilience" stat
content_md:
The new pvp gear has -crit damage and -dot damage taken stat and it's quite high, completely negating crits for many classes with 1.5x modifier, so a crit is same dmg as normal hit.

It massively reduces DoT damage pressure, and gives pvp sets a huge advantage vs pve tier sets.

This is OK, somewhat if the goal is to reduce burst, mission accomplished.

Then the devs throw a 20% and 30% dmg debuff on top, and now basically you destroy balance even worse.

Many classes rely on short burst windows, due to cooldowns, CC limitations, in order to succeed. Because once their burst & CC is gone, they become sitting ducks. While some classes are designed more for endurance, sustained dps, self healing mechanisms are basically buffed big time.

Remove the pvp dmg debuff. The new PvP gear is already a big step in right direction, though it needs some stat tuning or more creative bonuses. Having -crit dmg -dot already achieves goal of less burst damage. Do not double dip with another stat debuff.

As far as getting the instances. Turtle doesn’t have to release a thing. The clients everyone is using as we speak has the full layout of every instance and every terrain change they made that is actually permanent in that spot. All other servers need to do is load up the maps they have in the current client and it’s there.

What it won’t have is the mobs spawn points, loot tables, pathing, mechanics, or AI. But that is all stuff that would almost certainly change regardless of what another server does to match the theme of their stuff unless they were just cloning turtle entirely.

So, Epoch and any other server can copy this entirely just by keeping a copy of the TurtleWoW client to look at. Turtle doesn’t really have to do anything and couldn’t even stop others if they tried so blizzard would be hard pressed to hold that against them.

You have online databases of the mobs in them and their loot tables and YouTube videos showing many of the fights and pathing all to copy what they wanted. Not much other servers could possibly want that they can’t already get except maybe even easier access.

And if you want to give them easier access, just make videos stealthing through instances to show how mobs path though it as well as which have the true sight buff to the stealth and of the fights and post them online. There ya go and opens no one up to any increased legal liability.

subject: Allow owning unlimited Unique items for crafting/storage
content_md:
I suggest allowing players to own Unique items in any quantity for crafting and storage purposes, keeping the restriction only on equipping them.

author: Wolfmanpaulx
subject: Remove full spellschool immunities
content_md:
Remove full spell school immunities and replace them with resistance caps: up to 350 for fire elemental-based raid bosses like Ragnaros, 300 for fire red/black dragon raid bosses, and 250 for other fire-based raid bosses.

Additionally, change mob and trash fire immunities into resistance caps: 200 for elementals, 150 for dragons, and 100 for other creatures.

PS: "Numbers can be adjusted, based on tests and effective spell-pene capabilities"
PS2: "Should be taken alongside with other full immunities for other spellschools for example nature immunities of Emerald WB dragons"

This would give spell penetration a new important role and make fire spell school gear and fire-based raid builds viable. At the moment, there are spellhance fire-based builds, Immolate-Conflagrate Warlocks, Fire Mages, etc.

This should be applied consistently across every spell school in the game, effectively removing hard spell immunities by replacing them with high resistance values—capped at 350 for raid bosses, and minimally at 250. For trash and mobs, caps should range from 200 down to 100 depending on creature type.

This change would significantly improve the PvE caster experience by preventing situations where players are heavily punished by immunity mechanics, leaving them unable to contribute damage and forced to abandon their chosen builds and respec into specs they did not originally prefer.

This would also mean that Curse of Elements and other spell resistance debuffs/tools would gain niche value. While currently players are able to stack at least ~180 spell penetration passively from gear (with even higher values possible in later gearing), under this system the hardest resistances would likely still result in around a 70% DPS reduction even at high optimization.

The argument isn’t that frost should deal extra damage because it’s a “counter.” The point is that there should always be some possibility to deal damage, regardless of the element.

Using real-world physics or chemistry as an argument against change doesn’t really hold up here. If we follow that logic consistently, it quickly falls apart. What matters isn’t just the element or material itself—it’s the force, energy, and interaction behind it.

By that reasoning, even something made of fire could still be affected by sufficiently strong or disruptive forces. So saying “fire vs fire = no effect” is an oversimplification, not true realism.

The real issue is not realism—it’s design philosophy.

The goal should be to make the game and raids accessible to all specs. That doesn’t mean everything must be equally strong, but it should always be playable. High resistances can act as a natural limiter, but they should be something players can work against—through gearing, spell penetration, and optimization—rather than a hard “you cannot participate” wall.

Spell penetration could fill that role very well, similar to how armor penetration scales for physical damage. Instead of removing mechanics, this approach would deepen them—turning resistance into something you interact with, rather than something that simply shuts you down.

author: Lane13
subject: Dark Reaver of Karazhan summoned boss
content_md:
The summoned version of the Dark Reaver of Karazhan spawns in an area often traversed by players. Due to the easily accessible Karazhan 10 raid, people will come across the item to summon the world boss, complete the quest and leave it there due to ignorance or griefing.

So when an actual raid is formed to kill the boss, there's usually a tagged version standing on the spot and being aggroed all the time. Summoned world bosses despawn after 30 minutes of no action, which is essentially almost impossible for this one due to the spot it's in, because players accidentally bump into him and aggro.

The previous two kills of this boss that I've done went very well because we submitted tickets to the GMs kindly asking to remove the tagged mob, and they did. However, GM Septentrion refused to remove the boss today, citing the 30-minute rule that can realistically never be met in this case.

Another player wrote a ticket asking for help and a GM decided to move the boss away but not kill it. Therefore, we tried summoning a new one and couldn't because only *one* can be active at a time. This meant that we lost the summoning item and thus, the chance to kill the boss. You cannot even kill the tagged mob, as doing so will give you a lockout for the rest of the week, not letting you loot any items from new kills.

I thought the quality of TWoW and its GMs was better than this. Considering how poorly placed the boss is, why can't they just remove the tagged mob that is obviously not going to be killed by anyone instead of negatively affecting players like this? Every single time I tried to make a raid for the Dark Reaver, there was also a griefer constantly pulling the boss to reset the timer and disrupt the forming raid, which is obviously done on purpose. They could even summon a new one when they see there's a group forming and block the attempt as long as they have a summoning item.

I hope both the GMs and TWoW reconsider how they tackled this situation today because it was nothing short of Blizzard-like "support" on an otherwise excellent server.

author: Zvyrhol
subject: Re: AV desperately needs a time limit
content_md:
No, AV doesn't desperately need time limit. Time limit is contrary to the design of this battleground. "Pre-nerfed" AV from patch 1.5 was peak PvP experience in its own way. If you add time limit of, let's say, 30 minutes to the battleground that was designed to be played for hours/days, you kill 90% of content it has to offer.

How can you summon infantry, cavalry, Ice Lord or upgrade units to Champion in 30 minutes long game?
What's the point of time limit then? What issue does it solve? I see only honor/hour issue but it's not good solution because it makes more harm than good. If honor in turtle games is a problem for you, (I agree honor in turtle games sucks!), then there should be some fix that affects turtle games ONLY. The solution that butchers AV even more isn't good.

I'm afraid you have no idea of WoW history and yet you pretend you do. AV was the first battleground in WoW but it wasn't mean to be instanced during development, actually. In game files, you can find unused flight points to Alterac Valley. AV was originally meant to be warzone, something like Wintergrasp from WotLK but available 24/7. In patch 1.5 average AV game lasted for days until server reset. Even though it was instanced, it gave feeling that you were on never-ending war. Turtle AV represents this kind of experience.

Turtle is the only private server in the world that runs pre-nerfed version of AV. It's unique experience that we should preserve. Fast AV is aberration.

With ebb and t3.5 the cast speed is too slow for low hp mobs, but fine on bosses, but it's in pvp where we rly see the issue of the very long cast time. It has too many easy counters, with no real setup and not big enough impact especially with the easily dispelled moonfire.

I understand they don't want to go back to the old SF, but making it closer to 2.5 rather than 3 sec cast makes a lot of sense and for the love of everything that is unholy remove the extra second cast time of Barkskin, we have 70% pushback protection and owlkin frenzy gives us 30%, which means we get an extra 1 sec cast time for basically nothing.

You also can't make a cd on moonfire while having BoaT as a system, not to mention we don't have enough spells for that to be a thing either. Moonfire does 354-394 direct dmg on non-crits, it's not a problem.

Between Moonfire and Wrath, Moonkin of all classes has two decent fast casting spell options. Starfire was designed as a slow, very hard hitting nuke spell. author: Wolfmanpaulx
subject: Rogue bleeds and not often used talents
content_md:
Smoke Bomb, as one of the first Subtlety toolkit talents, is not performing as intended and is extremely rarely situational, which results in it being unused in most Subtlety builds.

Current state:
 35 energy, 8 yards radius, 8 sec duration, and a 20% chance for all targets inside to either be hit or to successfully hit.
It was originally intended as a PvP anti-caster defensive cooldown for situations where you are rooted, and Vanish or other root breaks (such as Improved Sprint) are on cooldown.

However, in practice, you can still get hit and pressured inside it to the point where it does not meaningfully change the outcome of a fight. Because of this, it often feels like the effect is not impactful enough to justify its usage.

On top of that, it has a 5-minute cooldown, which is quite high for a situational utility ability with inconsistent defensive value.

Proposed redesign idea:
 35 energy, 8 yards radius, 8 sec duration.

Instead of modifying hit chance inside the smoke, I would suggest shifting its identity toward a clearer offensive/utility window for Subtlety:

Increase damage of bleeds/DoTs by ~10% for targets affected by Smoke Bomb during its duration.
This would create a controlled 8-second pressure window where Subtlety can amplify Garrote, Rupture, poisons, and other bleed/DoT effects. Given that most DoTs tick roughly every 2 seconds, this would effectively enhance around 3–4 ticks during the window, which keeps the overall damage increase noticeable but not overwhelming, especially considering the 5-minute cooldown.

In addition, to preserve the original defensive intent of Smoke Bomb and improve its PvP usefulness:

Apply ~15% direct physical and magical damage reduction to targets inside the smoke.
This reflects the intuitive idea that visibility and precision are reduced inside a smoke cloud, making direct hits less effective and AoE pressure more effective. It would also help mitigate burst situations, while still allowing counterplay through positioning and control.

An additional talent that does not reflect current Subtlety tree usage, nor any modern Rogue build design (outside of some very old experimental “Rogue tank” concepts), is Blinding Haze.

Current state:

Blinding Haze reduces the energy cost of Distract by 5/10/15, and targets affected by Distract have their chance to hit reduced by 2/4/6% for 6 seconds.

In practice, this talent is rarely picked up by most players. The energy reduction is effectively negligible in real gameplay, since 15 energy is roughly one passive energy tick and Distract itself is already a situational tool used mainly for repositioning, crowd control setup, or pulling mobs safely. In most cases, Rogues already have enough time to wait for energy regeneration before opening, meaning this reduction does not meaningfully change gameplay decisions.

The additional 2–6% hit reduction is also extremely low impact. Even when fully talented, it is not strong enough to justify a 3-point investment, except in very niche scenarios such as large AoE trash pulls (5+ mobs), which is not something Rogue gameplay is primarily designed around due to having only limited passive cleave options.

Design context issues:

Looking at current Subtlety design, several core abilities already define the spec’s damage structure:

Rupture is mostly tied to Taste for Blood, which effectively incentivizes its use by converting combo point expenditure into a physical damage increase (~2% per combo point during its duration). Without this interaction, Rupture would have significantly less relevance in most rotations.
Garrote is often used by non-dagger Rogues mainly because there are limited alternative openers in PvE, especially since many raid mobs are immune or resistant to crowd control effects like Cheap Shot.

As a result, both bleeds are already somewhat “forced” into the rotation for mechanical reasons rather than purely synergistic design.

Proposed redesign direction:

A more meaningful direction for a talent like Blinding Haze would be to shift it away from minor utility modifiers and instead reinforce the natural synergy between Rogue bleed effects.

For example:

When Garrote and Rupture are both active on the same target, their interaction becomes amplified, increasing tick rate by:

 33% / 66% / 100% (based on talent points)

This would effectively reduce their duration by 1 / 2 / 3 seconds (based on talent points), creating a synchronized bleed pressure window.

Design intent:

This change would encourage deliberate stacking and timing of bleed effects, reinforcing Subtlety’s identity as a spec that builds controlled pressure through sustained effects rather than relying on flat, passive bonuses or low-impact utility modifiers.

It also aligns existing mechanics (Garrote + Rupture already being part of baseline rotations) into a more coherent system where combining them creates meaningful payoff, instead of simply being individually “required but uninspired” buttons.

author: Wolfmanpaulx
subject: Re: Rogue bleeds and not often used talents
content_md:
> **Crake wrote: Thu Apr 16, 2026 7:21 am**
> Openers in pve arent worth the time it takes to set them im, i’d rather just start sinister striking 2 seconds earlier, and be an energy tick, 2gcds and 2 seconds of auto attacks ahead of my peers

Ye, that’s also a fair point regarding openers in PvE.

My intention isn’t to slow gameplay down with setup, but to address two “dead spots” in the Subtlety tree and make existing tools interact in a more meaningful way.

Right now, both Smoke Bomb and Blinding Haze feel like low-impact picks:

Smoke Bomb is too unreliable defensively for a 5-minute cooldown
Blinding Haze provides negligible value in real scenarios

At the same time, Garrote and Rupture are already part of the rotation, but they don’t meaningfully interact—they’re used because systems require them, not because combining them creates value.

The goal of the suggested changes isn’t to introduce burst scaling or new multiplicative stacking, but simply to:

create a short, controlled window (Smoke Bomb) where Subtlety can apply slightly more pressure
and make bleed effects feel connected rather than isolated buttons

From a PvE perspective:

This wouldn’t meaningfully affect short-lived trash (where frontloaded damage like Sinister Strike will still dominate)
But it would provide more consistent value on longer encounters where bleeds actually have time to tick

From a PvP perspective:

Bleeds are already naturally limited by resilience and regeneration
So even with improved interaction, they remain sustained pressure rather than burst

Overall, the intent isn’t to push extreme numbers, but to turn currently underused talents into something that supports a clearer Subtlety identity: controlled pressure through coordinated effects, rather than isolated abilities with little synergy.

The whole “just stack hit to make Smoke Bomb work” argument ignores how the game actually plays and what Subtlety is built around.

Yes, on paper you can push ~19% hit and reduce the downside. But that means heavily warping your gear around a stat that Sub barely values, just to make a **5-minute cooldown** feel less bad for a few seconds. Outside of that window, you’re simply weaker:

 * less crit / AP / agility → worse burst and finishers
 * worse survivability → harder resets
 * no real gain to Sub’s actual win condition (setup → control → execution)

And the core assumption is wrong anyway — that Smoke Bomb creates asymmetry.

It doesn’t.

Even if you negate your own penalty:

 * casters will still land spells
 * warriors / druids / paladins still connect with yellow abilities and bleeds
 * several abilities are effectively guaranteed to hit

So the idea that “you don’t miss while enemies do” just doesn’t hold in real PvP.

Also, you do realize other classes operate under the same or even better baseline hit conditions, right? This isn’t some unique advantage you’re unlocking — it’s a self-imposed handicap to keep up.

From a practical standpoint:

 * In PvP, its usefulness is extremely questionable — most players don’t get real value out of it
 * In PvE (especially raids), using it is more likely to get you facepalmed than praised — 35 energy + 5 min CD for negligible impact is borderline trolling

And more importantly — we don’t even need this kind of defensive gimmick in Subtlety.

What the spec actually benefits from is:

 * better synergy within the tree
 * meaningful DPS / CC / CP / energy tools
 * something that reinforces its identity instead of fighting it

Even the old Dust design had far more practical use cases in both PvP and PvE.

At this point, if Smoke Bomb can’t be meaningfully improved without forcing players into awkward stat stacking, it would honestly be better to just replace it with the old Dust. It was simpler, but actually usable — and that already makes it a stronger design.
Or rewritte it into MH trinket - AoE stunn, shorter cd + stealth..... 'Deepwood Pipe'

content_html:
Smoke Bomb, as one of the first Subtlety toolkit talents, is not performing as intended and is extremely rarely situational, which results in it being unused in most Subtlety builds.

Current state:
35 energy, 8 yards radius, 8 sec duration, and a 20% chance for all targets inside to either be hit or to successfully hit.
It was originally intended as a PvP anti-caster defensive cooldown for situations where you are rooted, and Vanish or other root breaks (such as Improved Sprint) are on cooldown.

However, in practice, you can still get hit and pressured inside it to the point where it does not meaningfully change the outcome of a fight. Because of this, it often feels like the effect is not impactful enough to justify its usage.

On top of that, it has a 5-minute cooldown, which is quite high for a situational utility ability with inconsistent defensive value.

Proposed redesign idea:
35 energy, 8 yards radius, 8 sec duration.

Instead of modifying hit chance inside the smoke, I would suggest shifting its identity toward a clearer offensive/utility window for Subtlety:

Increase damage of bleeds/DoTs by ~10% for targets affected by Smoke Bomb during its duration.
This would create a controlled 8-second pressure window where Subtlety can amplify Garrote, Rupture, poisons, and other bleed/DoT effects. Given that most DoTs tick roughly every 2 seconds, this would effectively enhance around 3–4 ticks during the window, which keeps the overall damage increase noticeable but not overwhelming, especially considering the 5-minute cooldown.

In addition, to preserve the original defensive intent of Smoke Bomb and improve its PvP usefulness:

Apply ~15% direct physical and magical damage reduction to targets inside the smoke.
This reflects the intuitive idea that visibility and precision are reduced inside a smoke cloud, making direct hits less effective and AoE pressure more effective. It would also help mitigate burst situations, while still allowing counterplay through positioning and control.

An additional talent that does not reflect current Subtlety tree usage, nor any modern Rogue build design (outside of some very old experimental “Rogue tank” concepts), is Blinding Haze.

Current state:

Blinding Haze reduces the energy cost of Distract by 5/10/15, and targets affected by Distract have their chance to hit reduced by 2/4/6% for 6 seconds.

In practice, this talent is rarely picked up by most players. The energy reduction is effectively negligible in real gameplay, since 15 energy is roughly one passive energy tick and Distract itself is already a situational tool used mainly for repositioning, crowd control setup, or pulling mobs safely. In most cases, Rogues already have enough time to wait for energy regeneration before opening, meaning this reduction does not meaningfully change gameplay decisions.

The additional 2–6% hit reduction is also extremely low impact. Even when fully talented, it is not strong enough to justify a 3-point investment, except in very niche scenarios such as large AoE trash pulls (5+ mobs), which is not something Rogue gameplay is primarily designed around due to having only limited passive cleave options.

Design context issues:

Looking at current Subtlety design, several core abilities already define the spec’s damage structure:

Rupture is mostly tied to Taste for Blood, which effectively incentivizes its use by converting combo point expenditure into a physical damage increase (~2% per combo point during its duration). Without this interaction, Rupture would have significantly less relevance in most rotations.
Garrote is often used by non-dagger Rogues mainly because there are limited alternative openers in PvE, especially since many raid mobs are immune or resistant to crowd control effects like Cheap Shot.

As a result, both bleeds are already somewhat “forced” into the rotation for mechanical reasons rather than purely synergistic design.

Proposed redesign direction:

A more meaningful direction for a talent like Blinding Haze would be to shift it away from minor utility modifiers and instead reinforce the natural synergy between Rogue bleed effects.

For example:

When Garrote and Rupture are both active on the same target, their interaction becomes amplified, increasing tick rate by:

33% / 66% / 100% (based on talent points)

This would effectively reduce their duration by 1 / 2 / 3 seconds (based on talent points), creating a synchronized bleed pressure window.

Design intent:

This change would encourage deliberate stacking and timing of bleed effects, reinforcing Subtlety’s identity as a spec that builds controlled pressure through sustained effects rather than relying on flat, passive bonuses or low-impact utility modifiers.

It also aligns existing mechanics (Garrote + Rupture already being part of baseline rotations) into a more coherent system where combining them creates meaningful payoff, instead of simply being individually “required but uninspired” buttons.
I’d prefer something along the lines of:

Smoke Screen – 30 energy, 8-yard radius, 6 sec duration
Throws down a smoke bomb, silencing enemies and causing their attacks to miss.
MISS RATE: 60%

Which is kind of a hidden easter egg referencing the Rogue-type hero Riki from Dota 2.In my opinion, adds a lot of variation to both defensive and offensive game play, as well as in PvP and PvE situations.

author: Johnbradley01
subject: Shaman tanking and avoidance gear
content_md:
Hey

Shaman tanking is currently rough after item level 40 where most tanking pieces gets relagated to plate instead of mail.

Endgame, we have 1 set, and its not even a 8-piece, but the t2.5 from AQ40. You really have to be ultra sharp and spin a lot of plate to get 102.3% avoidance, even with kara40 gear. You need to stack everything possible and eat the problem of using lower statted gear with low overall stats. Compared with plate tanking, where the pieces in naxx are so fat with defensives stats you can run 70% tanking and run dps / threat pieces. If you look at the new timermaw hold plate tanking set, shaman could only dream about a set with so many stats and avoidance. We are shoe-horned into stacking str and agility (this is also what is on our t2.5 set) to quickly build up our earthen shield to survive, but we hardly use the str stat to block because there is almost no gear with +block chance available.

For example, for tanking gloves we have 2 options:
Rune Infused Gauntlets from Kara10 and Handwraps of Dead Winds from kara40. Handwraps are only high on the list because of the 28 agi. They are also leather, so a legit tradeoff on 100 armor and 0.6% avoidance loss from the Rune Infused.
Below these, there are 2 blue leather gloves with dodge on them from swv and DM.

Plate ofc has options in all tiers of content, from quests, to dungeons to entry raids all the way through all sets and into ultra lategame.

There are 6 belts with avoidance on them, all of them dodge, half them them leather. You also need to kill a world boss.

Proposed solution:
Instead of making more 1-class one-purpose gear, (plate gear with +healing, etc) give shamans access to plate gear in the enhancement talent tree with a "only 70 % armor contribution from plate pieces or something" It could be a line of requirements all the way from shield-specialization -> Ancestral Guardian -> Spirit Armor -> Plate Specialization if you want to avoid enhancement dps shamans just being auto plate users.

In the ideal world, every set on warrior and paladin with a tanking set, would also have a shaman equivalent that can be exchanged. Until that time, for the next redesign of tier sets, this could be a solution - also without cluttering up loot tables with even more snowflake drops.

Cheers
content_html:
Hey

Shaman tanking is currently rough after item level 40 where most tanking pieces gets relagated to plate instead of mail.

Endgame, we have 1 set, and its not even a 8-piece, but the t2.5 from AQ40. You really have to be ultra sharp and spin a lot of plate to get 102.3% avoidance, even with kara40 gear. You need to stack everything possible and eat the problem of using lower statted gear with low overall stats. Compared with plate tanking, where the pieces in naxx are so fat with defensives stats you can run 70% tanking and run dps / threat pieces. If you look at the new timermaw hold plate tanking set, shaman could only dream about a set with so many stats and avoidance. We are shoe-horned into stacking str and agility (this is also what is on our t2.5 set) to quickly build up our earthen shield to survive, but we hardly use the str stat to block because there is almost no gear with +block chance available.

For example, for tanking gloves we have 2 options:
Rune Infused Gauntlets from Kara10 and Handwraps of Dead Winds from kara40. Handwraps are only high on the list because of the 28 agi. They are also leather, so a legit tradeoff on 100 armor and 0.6% avoidance loss from the Rune Infused.
Below these, there are 2 blue leather gloves with dodge on them from swv and DM.

Plate ofc has options in all tiers of content, from quests, to dungeons to entry raids all the way through all sets and into ultra lategame.

There are 6 belts with avoidance on them, all of them dodge, half them them leather. You also need to kill a world boss.

Proposed solution:
Instead of making more 1-class one-purpose gear, (plate gear with +healing, etc) give shamans access to plate gear in the enhancement talent tree with a "only 70 % armor contribution from plate pieces or something" It could be a line of requirements all the way from shield-specialization -> Ancestral Guardian -> Spirit Armor -> Plate Specialization if you want to avoid enhancement dps shamans just being auto plate users.

In the ideal world, every set on warrior and paladin with a tanking set, would also have a shaman equivalent that can be exchanged. Until that time, for the next redesign of tier sets, this could be a solution - also without cluttering up loot tables with even more snowflake drops.

author: Cousinsmarsh
subject: My (Slightly) Drunken case for High Elf Druids <3
content_md:
Hello!  turtle_in_love_head

At an Ogre's face value, druids are traditionally associated with Night Elves and Tauren, and for very good reason.

Their cultures are deeply rooted in nature worship, the Emerald Dream, and the teachings of Cenarius. High Elves, on the other hand, are often seen as arrogant arcane purists, descendants of the Highborne who embraced magic over nature.

So why even consider this? **Prepare pitchforks**  insidious_turtle

Because Turtle WoW thrives on exploring the what if spaces in Warcraft lore, without breaking immersion. And High Elf Druids sit right in that juicy sweet spot   satisfied_turtle_head

Turtle has already expanded on lore in thoughtful ways, introducing new questlines, factions, and class combinations that feel authentic rather than forced. Sooooooo with that, there are a few important points to consider!

High Elves are descended from Night Elves. The capacity for druidic connection isn’t biologically or spiritually impossible, it’s culturally suppressed. High Elves have already demonstrated flexibility in their identity. Rangers, Priests, even adapting to human influence. A fringe group rediscovering druidism fits this pattern.

The overuse of arcane magic has historically led to catastrophic outcomes. It’s entirely believable that some High Elves would seek balance through nature, especially after witnessing the destruction tied to magic abuse.

This wouldn’t be about rewriting High Elf identity, it would be about exploring a forgotten branch of it    neutral_turtle_head

Our turtle High Elf Druids shouldn’t just be Night Elf Druids with different ears. They should have their own identity and aesthetic! Their druidism should reflect a fusion of arcane sensitivity and natural harmony. Think less primal wilderness, more refined ecological balance. This is brought on by the upcoming Quel’Thalas patch, seeing how the very nature has been destroyed by the Scourge.

These High Elves, aided by Night Elves, study methods how to cure their marred homeland.   turtle_tongue_head

Another point. High Elf racial gives a bonus to agility. A perfect match for a Druid   hiding_smth_turtle_head

Lots of good RP Potentials   turtle_in_love_head

![❗](//cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/twitter/twemoji@latest/assets/svg/2757.svg) Addressing Concerns ![❗](//cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/twitter/twemoji@latest/assets/svg/2757.svg)![❗](//cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/twitter/twemoji@latest/assets/svg/2757.svg)
This breaks lore![❗](//cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/twitter/twemoji@latest/assets/svg/2757.svg)![❗](//cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/twitter/twemoji@latest/assets/svg/2757.svg)![❗](//cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/twitter/twemoji@latest/assets/svg/2757.svg)

High Elves are about arcane, not nature.
That’s the dominant culture, but not every individual follows the norm. Warcraft has always allowed for outliers.

This steps on Night Elf identity![❗](//cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/twitter/twemoji@latest/assets/svg/2757.svg)![❗](//cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/twitter/twemoji@latest/assets/svg/2757.svg)![❗](//cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/twitter/twemoji@latest/assets/svg/2757.svg)

Only if implemented lazily. With proper differentiation, it actually highlights how different cultures approach the same discipline. I have faith in Turtle pulling it off   turtle_in_love_head

Final thoughts   hiding_smth_turtle_head

High Elf Druids aren’t about making the game easier or more convenient, they’re about deepening the world. They represent a bridge between arcane and nature, past and present, exile and rediscovery.

Turtle WoW has always excelled at taking risks that feel right. This is one of those ideas.

Curious to hear what others think, especially from a lore and RP perspective. Would you ever play a High Elf Druid? How would you envision their place in the turtle warcraft world?

Wishing you a good weekend   hiding_smth_turtle_head

Dear TurtleWow,
First off, I have very much enjoyed playing your server. Thank you for all the effort your team has poured into the development of the server. The changes and additions have presented a refreshing experience of a game I practically had memorized and allowed me to re-experience the game with the same wonder and excitement I felt many years ago when I was just a child. I know that I am not alone in this sentiment. Seeing that this server will come to an end is saddening, as its quality and content stood miles above other servers and even above the work of blizzard themselves. The love that the developers had for this game really shows through in the new zones, dungeons and quests. subject: Re: You guys should make your own MMO
content_md:
For a hackathon last year I've built a prototype for an event-based (immutable game state handoff) modular game server system, it's for card games but it can easily be repurposed for an MMORPG.

It could make development simpler and easier however it will probably be sluggish at any scale until it gets optimized.

This takes care of what a player can do in a game which is arguably one of the biggest challenges in making an MMORPG.

Then the only problems left are the game client (edit: done, see it in the subreddit) and the design/worldbuilding.

 -

I figure at least starting a community interested in making a custom MMORPG and seeing how far it can get might make sense -> <https://reddit.com/r/untitledMMORPG>

author: Skumbanana
subject: Re: Convert xp to money while xp gain is off
content_md:
So, this feature would appeal to:

 1. People who outpace their friends and want to play (alone or with them) while they catch up
 2. Twinks, who would get some money to help gear up
 3. Hardcores who want to stay hardcore
 4. Players who enjoy some specific zone or level bracket and want quests to stay relevant while retrieving some of the xp losses via money
 5. Say, broke players who don't have enough money to learn new skills and want to farm money doing quests (while maintaining their level), instead of grinding.

I myself am a mix of #1, #4, and #5

Not sure how much this would impact the economy. AH prices could go up a bit? I don't see this necessarily as a bad thing tho. Perhaps it would encourage players to take their time levelling and enjoy the wider content?

On the other hand, one could also argue that being able to turn off xp gain and being able to do, say, all level 40 quests while you are level 40 is reward enough for having xp off.

Still, overall, I think it would be a nice feature to have, with barely any impact on people who'd choose to ignore it.

author: Guunthar
subject: Ban self-boosting with multiboxxing
content_md:
I've encountered a few multiboxxers using a 60 mage to boost their characters in the open world.

They take their weak warrior alts on follow and scoop every single mob up in the popular aoe spots and arcane explosion them all easily, without any risk, and to the detriment of regular players trying to level for the first time.

Is this the kind of behavior that the community approves of? I personally found it very discouraging and it slowed down my own leveling a lot while I tried to sneak in a few tags around the unkillable 60 mage waltzing through the zone taking almost 0 damage.

I'll be honest I already don't exactly agree with the current multiboxxing rules as is but I think this kind of leveling is taking things too far. It is harmful to the experience of new players and it feels antithetical to the spirit of the server.

I understand boosting itself isnt outright banned, but shouldn't boosting on turtle wow be an occasional thing you help a guildie with instead of a full 1-60 grind where your warrior alt doesn't need to hit a single mob?

Hopefully the devs can implement a level difference check like SOM but in the mean time I hope you can agree that this sort of thing has no place on turtle.

They take their weak warrior alts on follow and scoop every single mob up in the popular aoe spots and arcane explosion them all easily, without any risk, and to the detriment of regular players trying to level for the first time.

Is this the kind of behavior that the community approves of? I personally found it very discouraging and it slowed down my own leveling a lot while I tried to sneak in a few tags around the unkillable 60 mage waltzing through the zone taking almost 0 damage.

I'll be honest I already don't exactly agree with the current multiboxxing rules as is but I think this kind of leveling is taking things too far. It is harmful to the experience of new players and it feels antithetical to the spirit of the server.

I understand boosting itself isnt outright banned, but shouldn't boosting on turtle wow be an occasional thing you help a guildie with instead of a full 1-60 grind where your warrior alt doesn't need to hit a single mob?

Hopefully the devs can implement a level difference check like SOM but in the mean time I hope you can agree that this sort of thing has no place on turtle.
I have encountred this twice actually and i just asked if i could have an invite for the quest i needed done and they were polite enough to invite me so i can get the kills i needed. Actually made the quest easier and quicker. Have you tried just asking for an invite?

author: Powrhouser
subject: New (lore-friendly) races for Druid
content_md: With the addition of Gilneas, I believe that human druids are a reasonable addition to the roster. Gilneas has always had deep roots in druidism with many harvest witches once inhabiting the area, and with Gilneas in ruins not only will a much higher influx of Gilnean refugees be expected to flock to the Alliance, but as well the desperate refugees will likely need to turn to their ancient ways to survive the trek to safe Alliance lands, akin to how many Draenei turned to shamanism out of necessity as they became broken. It only makes sense as well that these refugees would pass on some of their teachings to their Stormwind brethren. This could also give the TurtleWoW team a chance to experiment with some new and unique shapeshift models, either using existing animal models for the forms or possibly even making their own. What about the Horde, I hear you ask? The simple answer is give trolls the option to be druids as well, but if we want to be more experimental (and hear me out on this one)... Undead druids with plague bear/cat models for their shapeshifting. Unorthodox, yes, but with the Scourge and the Forsaken both being prevalent in the area of Silverpine, it's certainly a possibility that some Gilneans succumbed and were eventually freed from the Lich King's grasp, and nature magic, unlike the Light, doesn't necessarily reject Undeath.

author: Dracarusggotham
subject: Re: New (lore-friendly) races for Druid
content_md:
A lot of people are throwing shit at you, but I'll respectfully tell you the basics of Druidism here in WoW and why none of the things you're talking about are allowed:

Druidism is a custom unique to the Night Elves, or so it was until WoW's release, when they made the Tauren Druids just to balance the scales.

 1. Humans are a civilized race, built on faith in the Light. They can't be druids because simply... where did they come from?
 2. Humans originally practiced a very archaic form of shamanism and magic, which was further enhanced by the teachings of the High Elves in the war against the Amani. From there, the arcane side of humanity emerged. By now, humans probably don't even know they were once shamans, and they have no need to become one again, being able to be mages, paladins, or priests. 3. Trolls are only shamans, the faith of trolls is based on the Loa, they have no way to honor Mother Earth or Elune, which are the foundations of the druids, moreover, there is no race of troll that is known to have been druids, since they are always based on: Magic, Daemonism or Shamanism.

Finally, and quite separately, I'm a bit lacking in the lore of the Worgen, but I can tell you that here they are not druidic creatures or anything like that. They are creatures that were summoned from another dimension by the Archmage Arugal using the Scythe of Elune, and for the most part, I've seen that they are warlocks.

A lot of people have made their comments and I'm not gonna bash.  I'm just going to talk about the lore implications and add a recommendation of my own.

I don't believe that Worgen in classic lore have a confirmed origin, all we know is that they were summoned by a Gilnean archmage by the name of Archmage Arugal. And I believe the harvest witches, though a cool concept I like being a part of a lot of races subcultures, were not a thing until cataclysm sadly.

As far as Forsaken becoming druids because the light forsake them, I remembered something from the RPG books and have bad news on this lore direction.

"When Sylvanas Windrunner, Banshee
Queen of the Forsaken, regained her physical body, she
realized that the natural world would never respond
to her wishes again. Angered by this development,
she turned to arts that were becoming more and more
natural to her: necromancy."    Quote from the Dark Ranger section of the Horde Players Guide.

It is shortly followed up by another quote on the subject.

"  Converting from Elven to Dark
An elven ranger who dies and returns as a
Forsaken undergoes a great shock. She can no
longer cast elven ranger spells, and loses her
woodland stride ability. While some may choose
to let things be, most immediately seek out a dark
ranger to relearn their arts."

I read into it myself a little, but when it comes to the WarCraft RTS Games, the WarCraft RPG and then to WoW, things might become a little complicated:

We have a standardized version of the Druid here in WoW, but when you read through the different druid variants, you might quickly notice, that druidism (according to the RPG) doesn't always comes down to shapeshifting. But the shapeshifting is a big part of what the WoW-druid is.
From what i learn there and when we draw parallels to the Wildhammers, it seems like we have the variant of a "Lone Druid", which is more like a D&D Druid who talks to animals and have animals as companions (in Wildhammer case: Gryphons). When we break it down to the dwarves as playable race, we could fit those descriptions into the Hunter class from the game.

It's rather tricky to get lore and game mechanics aligned to each other.
(I made a statement about priests somewhere in the forum where i mentioned, that we have a pretty standardized form of the priest here on Turtle and that the priest actually "should" be something different, depending on the race/faith.)

So from my understanding the Wildhammers "Druidism" is a very basic one that wouldn't align with the druid we have in the game. I would even go so far to say, that Nightelves and Wildhammer Dwarves might have a different concept of druidism(?).
Regarding shamanism i wasn't able to find much, but from what i got this far, i assume that the Wildhammer concept of "shamanism" wouldn't align much with what we have in the game either.

From what i learn there and when we draw parallels to the Wildhammers, it seems like we have the variant of a "Lone Druid", which is more like a D&D Druid who talks to animals and have animals as companions (in Wildhammer case: Gryphons). When we break it down to the dwarves as playable race, we could fit those descriptions into the Hunter class from the game.

It's rather tricky to get lore and game mechanics aligned to each other.
(I made a statement about priests somewhere in the forum where i mentioned, that we have a pretty standardized form of the priest here on Turtle and that the priest actually "should" be something different, depending on the race/faith.)

So from my understanding the Wildhammers "Druidism" is a very basic one that wouldn't align with the druid we have in the game. I would even go so far to say, that Nightelves and Wildhammer Dwarves might have a different concept of druidism(?).
Regarding shamanism i wasn't able to find much, but from what i got this far, i assume that the Wildhammer concept of "shamanism" wouldn't align much with what we have in the game either.

Trolls are only shamans, the faith of trolls is based on the Loa, they have no way to honor Mother Earth or Elune, which are the foundations of the druids, moreover, there is no race of troll that is known to have been druids, since they are always based on: Magic, Daemonism or Shamanism.

Finally, and quite separately, I'm a bit lacking in the lore of the Worgen, but I can tell you that here they are not druidic creatures or anything like that. They are creatures that were summoned from another dimension by the Archmage Arugal using the Scythe of Elune, and for the most part, I've seen that they are warlocks.
I want to point out that Trolls are only Shamans due to the limitations of WoW. Trolls prior did not practice Shamanism in regards to the elements like the Orcs or even into ancestral spiritualism like the Tauren. They worship the Loa directly for their dark magic and use it to practice Voodoo with its living sacrifices and hexes. Blizzard simplified these vaguely similar concepts into one class for them to share by giving them trollish wards (which they renamed to totems to fit inline with Taurens), Tauren spiritualism (res and reincar, and twow with Spirit Link), and Orcish Elementalism (Shocks, Lightning, Weapon imbues).

Class design is meant to accommodate the game. Lore is just to make it make sense. We can suspend our disbelief as long as the implementation is good.
A similar case to what happened with the undead priests, many question why an undead can use holy magic when it is known that the Forsaken are entirely shadow priests.

And with the troll priests, we know that they are the equivalent of a Witch Doctor.
