author: Wafflecrusher
subject: PvP server is a bad idea, HC server is a good one
content_md:
I'm making this post in response to the two or three Pro-PVP spammers who won't stop flooding the forum. Although the responses to those posts, and responses to discord rabbling is reflective of the general attitude, I felt an independent post was necessary.

The EU population is not high enough to support a PVP server. I do not think the new patch will attract enough players to then justify a PVP server. I've attached population statistics below.

<https://turtlecraft.gg/#/population-graph>

I do not think the Pro-PVP players realize that the PVP server will only have world PVP for about ~6 months, at which point it'll only be one faction and world PVP will be gone. Then the PVP server will melt away, while still demanding resources which could be focused on the main realm. It's likely once the population shrinks enough, people with 60s on that realm will begin to demand transfers, requiring resources which could be used elsewhere. I also don't think the Turtle team should be opening and closing servers regularly (something people will start calling for in a few months when the faction imbalance gets out of hand). I do not think a PVP server will solve any existing problems, indeed it will potentially create many more.

I think a HC only server is something that I think would benefit everyone. No longer would players get frustrated when trying to group with someone who's tagged a mob, only to get the "sorry, this is a HC player" notification in red. HC players would get their own AH, and could trade freely. Additionally, it's a good way to mitigate future queues in the event there is population growth.

I do not see any long term benefit to a PVP server, indeed many problems could arise from it. I think a PVP server could be considered if the population doubles or triples, but now is not the time for a PVP server. A HC server on the other hand would solve many problems that currently exist. The philosophy of Turtle is slow and steady, I think the focus should be on solving long-term problems.

- Securing tag on worldbosses will not be guarantee for raid to get loot from it. Since everyone will be flagged, enemy raid could attack during fight and wipe raid with wb tag.

author: Tendies
subject: New PvP realm is still stupid
content_md:
I outlined almost two weeks ago why a new PvP realm is stupid: [viewtopic.php?t=9809](https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?t=9809)

Since then a new SEA PvP realm has been released, so I am going to further elaborate on why a new EU PvP realm is bad.

 - The new SEA realm has no crossfaction, so it must be assumed a new EU PvP realm wouldn't have it either. I outlined almost two weeks ago why a new PvP realm is stupid: viewtopic.php?t=9809

Since then a new SEA PvP realm has been released, so I am going to further elaborate on why a new EU PvP realm is bad.

- The new SEA realm has no crossfaction, so it must be assumed a new EU PvP realm wouldn't have it either. As I touched on in the previous post this is a nightmare for dungeon and raid balance because now you have to balance this stuff for groups with no paladins or no shamans or certain racials like fear ward.

- The battleground community (the real PvP'ers) will be split over two realms unless you enable cross realm battlegrounds. Problem with that is PvP'ers on the main Turtle realm will have vastly better access to gear with the crossfaction raid groups, where it will be both easier to get into a raid group and clear the raid for gear. Naturally, once people on the PvP realm wants to start BG'ing they'll either demand transfers or reroll to the main realm so they can get gear.
If you don't enable crossrealm BGs then you will split the already very small BG community, essentially killing it. And we already know PvP servers converge towards one faction dominance so BGs will be dead there as well. Basically a lot of new people who would enjoy BGs will be lured into levelling on the new PvP server and then quit once they find out BGs are dead and they should have rerolled to main realm, so you'll starve BGs of new people.

- And since the PvP realm won't have the 30% XP boost from war mode then it will further incentivise people to reroll to the main realm.

- I think it should be noted that the people who are begging for PvP realm are not PvP'ers. Just look at them, their profiles and discord names, they don't play battlegrounds, they are war mode levellers, they will stop playing or level a new character as soon as they hit 60. End-game is gonna be dead.

That is because this is final. There have been many (fresh) PvP servers so we know exactly what will happen. And Turtle just releasing a realm without any forethought would be incredibly dumb considering we do not know what effect it will have on the main realm... but why would you care? You said you do not play on Turtle but on Blizz servers after all...

So Turtle devs, please do not release a new realm, as others have said the queues are now fine despite transfers not being open yet. It will split the Turtle community. It will invite people who do not care about Turtle and will just play on the PvP server for a few months until it is gank city, one faction and dies. It will increase the PvP whining and make the community more toxic. It will force PvP balance changes on the RPvE players.

How many had horizontal progression? How many had persistant world goals?

And how many died from internal dev drama?

content_md:
Can the turtle team manage a pvp server and all of the issues that will arise from it? Sure. It may be a huge pain, and not deliver the kind of experience people expect, and will draw a huge amount of resources, but yes. They can probably tackle all of the issues that will inevitably arise from a PvP server. Should they? No.

The dev team should instead focus on solving problems that already exist, the animosity between the HC and non HC players for example. Or the constant server restarts and shutdowns. Or the various quests that bug out. Or launching the new patch. Or the bugs that will come from launching the new patch. Or developing new content. The list goes on.

In my opinion a PvP server is a bad idea, and the dev team should focus on other things. The first post here, and his previous post summarize the issues aptly.

author: Daedric
subject: Re: New PvP realm is still stupid
content_md:
People don't seem to understand that some who prefer PVP servers came to Turtle because Warmode is the best option for PVP , given the competition (that was my case at least.) Given the chance I'd 100% have gone onto a strictly PVP server and let PVE'ers and those who want to play HC be. They're fully entitled to a server which had settings they enjoyed from the start of the project- PVP-prefering individuals are the ones who needed to adapt because all of the other options, quite frankly, were garbage. As someone who has been on most of the large, previous vanilla-WoW private servers, Turtle WoW has a solid team and vision.

I'm fairly new to the server (relatively), but it seems the team has had to shift their priorities to accommodate a massive influx of new interest. That's to be expected.

Considering the flak Warmode seems to have gotten, it could even make sense for the Dev team to remove it so the OG realm could go back to the PVE/HC elements, and then have the separate PVP server. Then make the PVP servers have cross-realm battlegrounds/etc, and there you go. Maybe even link all realms in battlegrounds. Balancing is a whole 'nother issue.

I don't fully understand the rather narrow and selfish "you shouldn't have a PVP server" mindset when, ultimately, it will detract very little from the OG server in the long term. Yes, it's a departure from the Team's past statements, but some changes are to be expected when faced with a massive demand. Ultimately, you'll get a healthy population enjoying the culture on each. PVE/HC and PVP have vastly different goals. As was the case with Blizzard servers, let each type of gamer have their fun, and potentially link the battlegrounds to ensure stability.

author: Ishilu
subject: Alterntive to a HC server
content_md:
A lot of HC-vs normals drama comes form competition over quest mobs and the problem normally arises for named mobs (Zalazane, Tazan, Hogger etc.).

My idea:

Let HC players team up with normals under the following conditions:

 1) reasonable level range, +/-5 should be fine, so boosts are less likely to happen.
 2) short duration only. One minute should be fine, since it's enough to kill any named quest mob.
 3) long cooldown, I'm thinking of 30 minutes, to prevent hc's from "cheating" too much. Just give the HC a debuff "can't team up with normals" for that duration and they won't burn their big cooldown for killing some random trash mobs.

subject: Bring back the starter guilds
content_md:
So, let's break this down. <Newcomers> and <Still Alive> are disbanded.... Why? This makes no sense. Just stop moderating them, and leave them alone. No player is forced to remain in them, especially with the advent of the HC channel - which is a good call - but it itself is only a solution to anything if <Still Alive> remains... Alive.?. I took warmode, then disabled it, and then enabled it, wich makes me permanent warmode till 60.

Currently I'am at lvl 19, twinking my character.
I have chosen to be pvp enabled to have feeling like in old times, when I played vanilla, always on rppvp servers. Thrill of entering and questing in contested area is just great for me.

I did not choose it to have experience boost, I have also slow & steady and exhaustion.

I don't mind being ganked by higher levels, there were always those frustrated players that attack lower levels.

But I don't like when someone is safe in pve mode, and attack only if he is seeing an opportunity (for example, I'am at low health or surrounded by mobs). Ofc the same can be done by pvp enabled player, but in that case, with enough awareness I can fortreit, or sheep him etc. WIth pve guy, you never know if he just pass by or gonna attack you.

I think in this case, when someone enabled pvp, should have flag enabled for much longer.

法师AOE怪，这不是法师的职业技能造就出来的优势吗？每个职业不都有自己的优势吗？

小D可以变熊拉3个打，
骑士可以奉献拉5个打，
术士可以痛苦上debuff拉好几个打，
战斗贼可以开剑刃乱舞打2个，
牧师可以上debuff魔杖多个，

哪个职业没有这种本领？怎么就法师不能A了？那这样所有打2个怪的都封号算了。别TM搞双标

另外建议，取消所有职业特性，既然不需要职业特色，那就取消职业，所有人开局就TM一个职业选项：无用之人，进来大家都一样，也别互相BB。

 1、我TM觉得盗贼偷钱，这个职业特性特别不好，别的职业TM辛苦任务钱刚够学技能，盗贼凭什么就可以偷钱？就不受这个限制？我觉得盗贼偷钱特性，利于涉嫌RMT交易；

 4、等等

我觉得这样设计比较好，取消所有职业不需要的技能。比如，法师只有一个单体技能寒冰箭，盗贼只有一个影袭剔骨，猎人只能招宝宝射箭，牧师只有一个加血技能一个单体输出技能，等等

这样没有职业差别话，又公平，也省得都BB这那的？

subject: Improve or change Vagrant's challenge rewards!
content_md:
I think for the Vagrant's challenge, the rewards for completion at level 60 should be changed.

The title is fine as is, but the Mule that is rewarded is the same one from the donation store, and getting it as a reward doesn't feel as rewarding as you can get it through other means.

My suggestion is to change the Mule (bank pet reward) to either have a different model or a unique skin to distinguish it from the store one, or if it is too costly or time-consuming to make or change the assets for it, instead reward Vagrant players with 200 Turtle Tokens, similar to slow and steady, so they can at least get a pick of what reward or companion they want. I put this from the perspective of a HC player, as if you are running HC and Vagrant at the same time, you are likely never to use the Wanderer title and instead will use the Immortal/Inferno titles, making the companion/side reward more weighty by perspective. Thank you for taking the time to read this!

If you have your brainwashing device you can switch specs to 0/11/40 spec that gets holy nova and doesn't sacrifice any shadow damage, only a little mana regen.  Then pick yourself up a blade of eternal darkness (Mara princess is easy to solo as a shadow priest) and find the right downrank of holy nova that allows your mana to last through the fight you are engaging in.  Holy nova is easily one of the best AOEs in the game as it doesn't cause any threat and can be spammed with impunity immediately on pull.

Smite spec is also very viable on TWOW (although very gear dependent).  As a smite priest you can dish out very effective holy nova damage on aoe pulls in dungeons and raids. Just be prepared for full drinks, and/or mana consumables.

This isn't retail wow where everyone gets the same capabilities (homogenization... bleh). But if you're creative you can make do with the tools you have (or just think about rerolling an alt).

>
>   Right, right. Do you think that would be a good avenue, or maybe a method to spread dots?

I am in favor of ways for dot heavy specs/classes, hello affliction warlocks, to be able to spread their core dots more easily. Spending 6-30 cooldowns dotting up targets while some frost mage yoho CoCs, blizzards, then ice lance spams to top the dps charts does make me jealous. While leveling, Rain of Fire is nice but expensive and doesn't really fully come online until late 40s when you have enough points in Destruction to make it more efficient/powerful.

For a default 'Mind Sear' I think a directed aoe would probably be the best way, keep the base spell a simple aoe for newer players and whatnot. Then add/change a talent to give it the ability to spread SWP. Perhaps a new talent that costs 2 points that does it. Its implementation depends on what is possible in the engine's backend as much as it is on balance and gamefeel/fun. Note that neither implementation below will increase the duration/refresh SWPs duration on the main target of the spell.

Complex implementation: Migraine (2) - "When your Mind Sear deals damage and the main target is affected by your Shadow Word: Pain spell, all other targets affected by Mind Sear are inflicted with Shadow Word: Pain with a duration of 3 seconds. If the targets are already inflicted with Shadow Word: Pain then additional 3 seconds are added to Shadow Word: Pain's duration up to your Shadow Word: Pain's maximum duration. If the additional duration would increase the duration past the maximum duration, the duration is refreshed and the target takes 16/33% of Shadow Word: Pain's tick. Improved Shadow Word: Pain increases this damage to 25/50%." This means that after a single Mind Sear the other targets would have SWP duration at 11 seconds due to the 1 second per tick of the Mind Sear. The reason for it being an incremental duration increase is to prevent crazy damage burst or the player doing a single damage tick then cancelling the spell for a cheap/fast dot spread. The spriest will have to Mind Sear at least twice to get the duration high enough to proc the bonus damage on duration overflow. The Imp SWP bonus is because the talent gives 3/6 second greater duration and if we did not account for it then players would ignore that talent to get the earlier 33% damage tick procs. This is a bit of a wordy talent, but spriests already have things like Vampiric Touch and Shadow Weaving so they are used to reading.

Engine limited/Computationally simple implementation: Migraine (2) - "Casting Mind Sear for its full duration on a target inflicted with your Shadow Word: Pain has a 50/100% chance to cause a mental shockwave, inflicting other targets in its radius with Shadow Word: Pain. If the targets are already afflicted by your Shadow Word: Pain they take damage equal to 3 seconds of Shadow Word: Pain's damage." This implementation is likely the easiest to add, but could be bursty and lead to spriests pulling threat early. It does not refresh SWP on targets that already have it so they are taking damage at 3 second intervals plus the 5 second interval at the end of Mind Sear. (Not including player/server lag etc.)

There's probably dozens of other ways to implement it, but these are a good starting point. Extra input by spriest mains is appreciated.

Its implementation depends on what is possible in the engine's backend as much as it is on balance and gamefeel/fun. Note that neither implementation below will increase the duration/refresh SWPs duration on the main target of the spell.

Complex implementation: Migraine (2) - "When your Mind Sear deals damage and the main target is affected by your Shadow Word: Pain spell, all other targets affected by Mind Sear are inflicted with Shadow Word: Pain with a duration of 3 seconds. If the targets are already inflicted with Shadow Word: Pain then additional 3 seconds are added to Shadow Word: Pain's duration up to your Shadow Word: Pain's maximum duration. If the additional duration would increase the duration past the maximum duration, the duration is refreshed and the target takes 16/33% of Shadow Word: Pain's tick. Improved Shadow Word: Pain increases this damage to 25/50%." This means that after a single Mind Sear the other targets would have SWP duration at 11 seconds due to the 1 second per tick of the Mind Sear. The reason for it being an incremental duration increase is to prevent crazy damage burst or the player doing a single damage tick then cancelling the spell for a cheap/fast dot spread. The spriest will have to Mind Sear at least twice to get the duration high enough to proc the bonus damage on duration overflow. The Imp SWP bonus is because the talent gives 3/6 second greater duration and if we did not account for it then players would ignore that talent to get the earlier 33% damage tick procs. This is a bit of a wordy talent, but spriests already have things like Vampiric Touch and Shadow Weaving so they are used to reading.

Engine limited/Computationally simple implementation: Migraine (2) - "Casting Mind Sear for its full duration on a target inflicted with your Shadow Word: Pain has a 50/100% chance to cause a mental shockwave, inflicting other targets in its radius with Shadow Word: Pain. If the targets are already afflicted by your Shadow Word: Pain they take damage equal to 3 seconds of Shadow Word: Pain's damage." This implementation is likely the easiest to add, but could be bursty and lead to spriests pulling threat early. It does not refresh SWP on targets that already have it so they are taking damage at 3 second intervals plus the 5 second interval at the end of Mind Sear. (Not including player/server lag etc.)

There's probably dozens of other ways to implement it, but these are a good starting point. Extra input by spriest mains is appreciated.

author: Matiel
subject: Re: Mindflay x2
content_md:
Mind Flay:

As much as I'd like it to crit gameplay-wise, lore-wise it shouldn't be able to crit, as it isn't individual missiles like arcane missiles, but an ongoing assault on the targets psyche, it's a channeling dot. I think however that it should have it's spell coefficient increased to fixed 100%, with its baseline damage decreased to compensate. Ut is a direct shadow damage attack over time, not just a dot like sw:pain, applied and forgotten, or a one time cast like mind blast, so it should, in spite of its slowing ability, benefit more from shadow/spell damage bonus, making it more unique and allow some experimenting beyond stacking spirit and wanding during levelling.

AOE:

For Spriest AOE I'd much prefer something like the Mind Sear from WotLK, however applied to the self, so it deals shadow damage to enemy targets around the priest. A channeling AOE affecting all nearby enemies.

Shadow could include Frost damage, a kind of aura, that saps the life of nearby targets that take shadow damage, dealing frost damage to them, so dotting up multiple targets becomes a stronger aoe.

Easiest would be making a Shadow Nova from Holy Nova.

author: Sleeplust
subject: Changing the limit for accepting quests "The Fury Runs Deep" and "Powers Beyond"
content_md:
Currently (in December 2024), unlocking and accepting the quest "The fury runs deep" requires that you turn in the quest "The dark iron war". The problem or illogical part is that we unlock a lower-level quest in a dungeon suitable for players around level 26 after finishing an elite quest involving mobs over level 30.

"Powers beyond" is a quest for players of level 38 or higher requiring defeating the lich Amnennar the Coldbringer, level 41 final boss of Razorfen Downs. And the quest is accepted in Gilneas, a region for leveling from 40 to 48. Taking the quest at around level 43 just makes this quest feel too low for players busy leveling to consider doing it.

My suggestion is simple - enabling the quest The fury runs deep to be taken as an option parallel to The dark iron war. For Powers beyond, lower its level of acceptance to 37, equal to that of another quest "Bring the End", which requires defeating the same boss in the same dungeon. Another option could be moving the quest to a region around level 30 to 40, like Arathi Highland or simply deleting this quest.

author: Sagabal
subject: First-Aid solutions to non-poison debuffs while levelling
content_md: Currently if you get a long-lasting poison from a mob, you can either find another player to cleanse you or spend resources costing an uncommon drop from certain mobs to get rid of it.  On the other hand, if you get infected with some long-lasting disease or curse from a mob, you need to go find another player, and unless you have a restorative cure-all potion, that's it.  A dedicated way to remove low and mid level curses, diseases, or magic effects could provide an alternative for players still leveling, without stepping on the balance of purification and restorative potion's roles as the end game soft-green-echo-eyedrop-antidote cure-alls.

author: Lanning2023
subject: SMT (Shaman Tank) Balance Feedback & Enhancement Proposals
content_md:
Dear Turtle WoW Developers,

As a dedicated Shaman Tank (SMT) on the Asian server, I’ve successfully led raids through Naxxramas and Emerald Dream speedrun challenges with my guild **<North & South>**. While SMT is a thrilling role, I’d like to respectfully propose adjustments to address current limitations:

 ---

### **1. Survivability Issues**
 **Current Challenges**:
 - Compared to Paladins, Warriors, and Druids, Shamans lack reliable **active mitigation tools**.
 - In critical situations, we can only rely on **Stoneclaw Totem** (easily destroyed) or **Earth Shield** (limited absorption), leaving SMT overly dependent on healers during high-damage phases.

 **Proposed Solution**:
 - **New Talent: Enhanced Earth Shield**
 - **Effect**: Extend Earth Shield’s CD to 10 minutes.
 - **Damage Reduction**: Earth Shield reduces incoming damage by 30% when triggered.
 - **Synergy Bonus**: If triggered by **Lightning Strike**, increase its healing effect by 500%.
 - **Design Goal**: Provide burst survivability without overshadowing other tanks’ uniqueness.

 ---

### **2. Gear Availability Constraints**
 **Current Challenges**:
 - **Missing Tank Gear Slots**: Wrist, Hands, and Waist slots lack viable mail defense gear.
 - The only SMT waist item (*Stoneplate Waistguard* from world bosses) has a **4% drop rate**, creating excessive RNG dependency.
 - **Stat Balance**: To reach **400 Defense Rating**, SMT must sacrifice Stamina, resulting in only ~7,500 HP (below 40-man raid standards).

 **Proposed Solutions**:
 - **A. Introduce New Mail Defense Gear**:
 - Add Stamina/Defense Rating-focused items for Wrist, Hands, and Waist slots (e.g., crafted *Earthwarder Gauntlets* or raid drops).
 - Suggested Sources: Crafting recipes (Blacksmithing/Leatherworking) or mid-tier raid bosses (e.g., updated Zul’Gurub).
 - **B. Defensive Totem Additions**:
 - New totems providing raid-wide Defense Rating or Stamina buffs (e.g., *Totem of Unyielding Earth*).

 ---

### **3. Long-Term Vision**
Balancing SMT would:
 - Encourage more players to explore hybrid specs, enriching class diversity.
 - Align with Turtle WoW’s philosophy of empowering underutilized playstyles.

 ---

### **Closing**
Thank you for your incredible work in expanding the Vanilla experience! I’m passionate about perfecting the SMT role and would gladly provide further testing/data if needed.

Best regards,
 **Sweetheart Milk Bunny (甜心奶兔酱)**
 **Server**: Turtle WoW Asia
 **Guild**: North & South (南北)

author: Akos1896
subject: Re: SMT (Shaman Tank) Balance Feedback & Enhancement Proposals
content_md:
Hello!

I agree with point 2. There is for example a mail tanking 3piece set in AQ40 but it has item overlaps with the T2,5 set. I'd love to have that set redesigned to cover item slots which T2,5 doesn't cover (Fallen Prophet set if I recall well).
And even for earlier raiding: turning one of the early-raid sets into a tanking one would help a ton. Maybe ZG. Itemization is currently very poor for mail tanking.

For point one: while I'd love a defensive CD, the one you proposed seems too strong. If I know well elemental shields can't proc faster than 1,5 sec and with the shield talent, this becomes 2,5 sec. Even if you are under constant attack, you get a 30 percent mitigation with built in life gain for more than 20 seconds on a 10 min CD. Can work though, maybe I'm too paranoid. I'd raise its CD though.

For the devs: you made a tank build and gave it some support with raiding items.
Be a man and instead of telling things like 'we designed this as a dungeon tank' accept that you created a tank, it needs the full toolkit to work at every level. You made most of the job, what remains are some mail items yet to be created and a def CD.

author: Puxido
subject: Guild PVP
content_md:
Ok, clickbaity title so lets get to the point.

Since there are cross faction guilds and some people would probably enjoy doing pvp with their guildmates, it make be an interesting option to pvp as a guild.  And I'm not recommending some complex new system reinventing the guild system.

When you click to flag yourself as PVP, you have the option of instead of flagging to your faction, you flag to your guild.

If two guild masters are close to each other, they can right click each other as if doing a dual and ask to make the other guild "enemies".  It could also be done through the guild tab but either way the other GM has to accept.

I see this as mostly being something to be helpful with RP situations, though most use dice rolls to be honest.  But it'd be a cool way to set up or organize large scale pvp events between guilds, and it'd be a cool way for cross faction guilds to get together and pvp with their guildmates across faction lines.  If its more than two guilds getting in on this than it'd be a bit difficult to set up, unless you could flag your raid as pvp rather than guild but I don't think that'd work but here is another idea.

What if you could also flag yourself with "The black flag", a pvp option where your flagged against both factions.  Anybody from either faction can engage in pvp with you.  It'd also open up a cool idea for a new leveling challange.  Raise the black flag and declare yourself an enemy of all nations, and try to make it to level 60 with anybody from either faction being able to attack you.  Extra hard if your in Hardcore mode.

I like that Idea more to be honest, and it'd make 3 or more guild battles viable, just have to be careful not to hurt your teammates with area of effect attacks.
